ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> Eligible participants were adults aged 60 or older with MCI, defined by Petersen criteria as performance 1-2 standard deviations below age-and education-adjusted norms in at least one cognitive domain.

> All participants had preserved activities of daily living and no major psychiatric or neurologic comorbidities.

> Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive daily oral Li carbonate (150-300 mg, titrated weekly to maximum tolerated dose) or identical placebo, using permuted blocks stratified by Aβ-beta (Aβ) plaque status.

> All 21 PiB-positive participants had aMCI.

> Higher APOE4 protein levels in PiB+ participants are consistent with the greater proportion of APOE ε4 carriers in this group (60.0% versus 28.0% among participants with baseline plasma;

> In the placebo group, PiB+ participants had higher levels of p-tau217 (FDR = 0.033) and nominally higher levels of APOE4, GFAP, VCAM1, and p-tau231, and lower levels of several proteins, including ANXA5, MDH1, CD40LG, TARDBP, p-SNCA129, SNCA, CRP, and SOD1 (Supplemental Figure 1b).

> Overall, baseline protein differences between aMCI and non-aMCI participants were modest and did not survive multiple-testing correction.

> Baseline differential protein abundance by randomized treatment assignment and Aβ-PET status (A) Volcano plot (left) and selected protein distributions (right) comparing participants assigned to Li (LITH) versus placebo (PBO).

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

live_data_statements: Eligible participants were adults aged 60 or older with MCI, defined by Petersen criteria as performance 1-2 standard deviations below age-and education-adjusted norms in at least one cognitive domain.
All participants had preserved activities of daily living and no major psychiatric or neurologic comorbidities.

Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive daily oral Li carbonate (150-300 mg, titrated weekly to maximum tolerated dose) or identical placebo, using permuted blocks stratified by Aβ-beta (Aβ) plaque status.
Higher APOE4 protein levels in PiB+ participants are consistent with the greater proportion of APOE ε4 carriers in this group (60.0% versus 28.0% among participants with baseline plasma;

In the placebo group, PiB+ participants had higher levels of p-tau217 (FDR = 0.033) and nominally higher levels of APOE4, GFAP, VCAM1, and p-tau231, and lower levels of several proteins, including ANXA5, MDH1, CD40LG, TARDBP, p-SNCA129, SNCA, CRP, and SOD1 (Supplemental Figure 1b).
Overall, baseline protein differences between aMCI and non-aMCI participants were modest and did not survive multiple-testing correction.
